Parental bereavement leave is a day one right.

Reinstatement after armed forces service in Northern Ireland

Employees will be entitled to Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay as long as they were employed with their usual employer on the day of the bereavement. They do not need to have been continuously employed for 26 weeks up to the week before the one in which the child died, was stillborn or the date of the miscarriage. Expected earnings and reasonable assumptions about earnings can be used to determine eligibility.

Employee works for another employer

If your employee works for another employer during a week that they were claiming Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay from you, you need to check whether they were employed by that employer in the week before the child died or was stillborn, or the woman who experienced the miscarriage became aware of the miscarriage.

If your employee works for another employer, you need to check whether they were employed by that employer:

during a week in which they are claiming Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay

in the week before the child died or was stillborn, or the person who experienced the miscarriage became aware of the miscarriage

if they are an employee who satisfies the relationship criteria with a woman who has experienced a miscarriage

It’s up to your employee to tell you that they’re working for another employer.

If your employee is working for someone who employed them in the week before the child died or was stillborn, or the woman who experienced the miscarriage became aware of the miscarriage, you should continue to pay them Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay as normal.

If your employee is working for someone who did not employ them in the week before the child died or was stillborn:

you must stop paying Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay from the start of the week in which they work for the new employer

your liability to pay Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay in that week ends on the last day of the week Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay was paid before they started work for the new employer

you must give them the non-payment of Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay form

Keep a copy of the declaration of entitlement to Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay made by your employee. You may need to record this as evidence for subsequent periods of Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay.

Trade disputes or industrial action

If an employee takes part in industrial action or is absent because of a trade dispute during the period used to work out their actual earnings, this may affect their Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay.

Their average weekly earnings will be calculated using a lower income, which could mean they get less Statutory Parental Bereavement Pay.
